title: Part I: the swordfighting trial (fish, sword, troll, Smirk, insult fights, Carla)

entry.notes: S2 is not contiguous; it runs in four pieces inside S1. (1) Kitchen, moves 1-4: after S1 move 8 (enter the kitchen), before S1 move 9 (pot; the meat is S1 move 10). (2) Store, moves 5-8: move 5 (sword) after S1 move 47 (shovel) and before S1 move 52 (bell); moves 6-7 between S1 moves 53 (mint) and 54 (shovel); move 8 ('browse') between S1 moves 55 and 56, because S1 move 56 waits for var 32 eq 4 and with the sword paid only this choice ends the menu. (3) Block 1, moves 9-28: right after S1 move 83 (Lookout -> map; S1 owns that step, so the draft's duplicate 'Lookout -> Melee map' is removed): troll, Smirk, fight 1. S1 moves 84-96 (fork, forest, treasure, dig) follow; S1 move 84 must wait for move 28. (4) Block 2, moves 29-59: room 64 -> map (new: nobody owned it), fights 2-3 at the fork, forest to Carla, Carla, exit. This matches the record (fish and sword in S1's rooms; troll, Smirk and one fight before the treasure). The entry state below is the state at move 9: ego on the Melee map at 913's walk point (77,119), map entry 4 (Var[290]=4 after the entry script's increment), pirate 1 walking without a fight option. Inventory = S1's items at its move 83 plus the fish and the sword. Money 202 (478 - 100 map - 1 mint - 100 sword - 75 shovel); Smirk's '30 pieces of eight' needs Var[195]>30. Var[199]==0 means S1 never talked to the important-looking pirates (it changes Smirk's first option and the store's option 122). The rubber chicken 377 adds Smirk options after the ones used; no key changes. TEXT-SKIP CONVENTION: every line is skipped with '.' on the first frame that has an effect (bridge SPEEDRUN_SKIP_TEXT=1, default on in src/speedrun/engine.py; maybeInjectSkip in patches/0001-scumm-add-speedrun-bridge.patch). Without it every `until` is still reached, only later. If SPEEDRUN_SKIP_CUTSCENES=1 is also on, the bridge presses Esc itself once an override is armed: then drop the explicit Esc moves 14, 20 and 52, whose `after` may otherwise never be seen. BRIDGE C3 SEMANTICS (conditionHolds in the patch): var = _scummVars[N], bit = descumm Bit[N], room = _currentRoom (the forest pseudo-room in the forest, room.cpp:154), has = in inventory and owned by ego, state = object state. Var 3 VAR_HAVE_MSG, 4 VAR_ROOM, 32 VAR_VERB_SCRIPT. Var[194] is the dialogue choice: reset to 0 right before every menu wait and set to the chosen verb id (120-128) after Guybrush's line (global/script-014.txt [00F7]-[0105]); MENU = {var 194 eq 0}. Fight vars: Var[240] current insult, Var[262] exchanges lost and Var[263] won this fight, Var[282] fights won, Var[285] fight mode (3 pirate, 2 Sword Master). FIGHT PLAN (from the scripts; replaces the record's troll insult and save/reload): Smirk gives insults 2, 8 and comebacks 2, 8. A fight is won at 3 exchange wins before 3 losses (Var[351]=3; Carla 5). Guybrush insults first and the exchange winner insults next. Comeback 16 ('family reunion') answers Carla's 21, 32 and 33 (global/script-090.txt [0054]-[010D]), so comebacks {2, 8, 16} cover exactly 18, 21, 24, 32, 33, the five a 5-0 needs. Learning it costs two lessons: hear insult 16 from a pirate (fight 1), then use it on a later pirate who counters (fight 2). Fight 1 needs one turn-passing loss before the pirate can insult; a default insult (34-36) is a certain loss, so the troll's 'dog' is not needed. Total 12 pirate exchanges (5+4+3: 9 wins + 3 required losses) and a 5-0 Carla. STEERED OUTCOMES: every random outcome is chosen by delaying the preceding menu choice (rng_points). Only two are hard targets: fight 1 E3 must draw pirate insult 16, and fight 2 E1 must be countered. Every other target is a SET (pirate insult in {2, 8} or {2, 8, 16}; Carla insult among the answerable ones left), so the conditions are order-free (counts plus MENU) and never name the insult. REPLY-BY-INSULT MOVES (28, 33, 54-58): the right reply depends on the steered insult; the move's `choose` holds the planned instance and its note holds the table. The search resolves `choose` per seed from Var[240] at the menu (or the executor reads Var[240] and maps it through the table). A wrong reply loses the exchange, so the `until` fails and the executor raises RouteError instead of silently continuing. INTERCEPT MOVES (22; and 30, 36 when no fork-bound pirate comes): an encounter starts when, in a frame in which pirate actor A (8, 9 or 10) was still walking at the end of the previous frame, ego is not moving and getDist(ego,A) < 2 (Chebyshev <= 1) (room-085-melee/local-202.txt [018A]-[01A6]). Pirates walk at WalkSpeed(1,1) (up to about 2 px/frame in x on diagonals) along walkbox paths to 913 (77,119), 911 (72,87), 912 (133,87) or 910 (219,21), vanish for 0-120 jiffies (0-24 frames), reappear at a random destination (1 in 5: room 148, gone for this visit) and pick a new one ([01B0]-[024F]). Procedure: on a fork of the engine state, run the map forward with ego idle and record each pirate's per-frame position; choose a pirate A, a frame t at which A is still walking, and a stand point P within 1 px of A's position at t that ego can reach and stop at before t (ego walks at 1.99 px/frame, about 2.96 on slope 1.5:1 diagonals); P must lie outside every map object box (a click there is that object's Walk to) and inside a walkbox. Click P (one floor click, global/script-033.txt [0062]); the encounter comes at about t. Cost = map frames from the gate to the encounter. If none comes by t+5, re-plan from the current state with another pirate.
